systemPrompt:
You are an assistant helping a developer with their CircleCI projects. Answer the user's question using only the tools provided to you. Ground every claim in data you actually retrieved; if you cannot retrieve something, say so. Do not change anything in the project beyond what the user explicitly asks for. Finish with a clear, direct answer to the question.

The current directory is a checkout of the luisejroblesci/circleci-cli repository. You can inspect its files with the read-only list_files and read_file tools.

This server exposes CircleCI: the CI pipelines an org runs, the deploys those
pipelines produce, and the config, orbs and usage data around them. Every tool
acts as the authenticated user and sees only what that user can see.

Ids are UUIDs and are not interchangeable — a run id, a workflow id and a job
id are distinct, and a tool handed the wrong kind fails rather than guessing.
Nothing accepts a job number or a CircleCI web URL. Projects and orgs are the
exception: they take either a slug ("gh/org/repo", "gh/org") or a UUID.

SKILLS. This server ships written playbooks for the work that takes several
of the tools below — the orderings, the costs and the usual mistakes, which
no single tool description can carry:

    list_skills  the catalog: what each playbook covers, and its references
    get_skill    one playbook, or one of its bundled references

Before working through the tools below, call list_skills once and load any
skill whose description covers the work, together with the related skills it
names. It takes no arguments and returns the whole catalog, so that one call
is the entire search. If nothing clearly fits, load nothing and work from the
tool descriptions. One pass serves a whole session: having listed once, do not
list again.

A skill earns its call at the start of a piece of work, not after one has gone
wrong. The same guides are readable as resources under circleci://skills/ for
clients that browse resources rather than call tools.

PIPELINES. The tools form a chain, each level's id feeding the next:

    list_runs -> get_run -> list_run_workflows -> get_workflow -> list_workflow_jobs -> get_job

Enter at list_runs; it is the only one of these that takes a project rather
than a UUID. With no project named, mine=true lists the user's own runs across
every project. Skip levels whenever you already hold an id — get_run is
pointless if you have the run id and want its workflows.

DIAGNOSING A JOB. Five tools take a job id and answer different questions.
Which you pick matters more than the order:

    get_job                 which step failed, and its exit code
    list_job_tests          which tests failed
    get_job_logs            what a step printed
    get_job_resource_usage  whether it ran out of CPU or memory
    list_job_artifacts      the files it persisted, with download URLs

Start with get_job — it is cheap and names the failed step. If that step ran
tests, go to list_job_tests, which is far cheaper than logs and already
filtered to failures. Reach for get_job_logs only when you need the output
itself; it is the most expensive tool here, so keep tail_lines small. If a job
died with nothing in its logs, check get_job_resource_usage for an OOM.

DEPLOYS are a separate subsystem, keyed on projects and orgs rather than on
pipeline ids, and reachable without touching a run:

    list_deployments                what was deployed — to a project, or across an org
    list_deploy_components          a project's deployable units
    list_deploy_environments        an org's release targets (production, staging)
    list_deploy_component_versions  a component's version history
    get_deploy_component            one component by id
    get_deploy_environment          one environment by id

For "what is live" or "when did X ship", use list_deployments — pass project for
a single project or org for everything in the org. The two get_ tools resolve an
id you already hold back to its name; the list tools already return names, so reach
for them only when an id arrived from somewhere else.

CONFIG AND ORBS need no CircleCI resource at all; they work on YAML you hold:

    validate_config  compile a config and report its errors
    get_orb          an orb's published versions — whether a pin is stale
    get_orb_source   an orb's YAML — how to call its jobs and commands

Read an orb's source before writing config against it, and compile a config
before pushing it rather than after.

WRITES. rerun_workflow is additive: it creates a new workflow. cancel_workflow
stops running work. rollback_deploy_component redeploys production software.
Confirm with the user before calling any of them unless they asked for it
directly — and for a rollback, confirm the component, the environment and both
versions rather than just the intent.

Also: get_me for the authenticated user's identity and ids, and
download_usage_data for an org's billing CSVs (asynchronous — start an export,
then poll it).

When a tool errors, read the message before retrying. Most errors here say
what was wrong — the wrong kind of id, a missing project, an execution index
out of range — and the same arguments will fail the same way.

Target CircleCI project: gh/luisejroblesci/circleci-cli (organization: gh/luisejroblesci).

version: 2.1

parameters:
  setup_go:
    type: string
    default: github.com/circleci-functions/setup-go@v0.5.1-684fd5b

commands:
  setup:
    steps:
      - checkout
      - install-go
      - install-task

  # Installs the toolchain and restores the module, build and lint caches, saved at job end.
  install-go:
    steps:
      - run: circleci run << pipeline.parameters.setup_go >> --
          --version-file go.mod
          --golangci-lint-cache
          --checksum '{{ checksum "go.sum" }}_{{ checksum "clikit/go.sum" }}_{{ checksum "tools/go.sum" }}'
      - run: go version

  install-task:
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Install go-task
          command: |
            sh -c "$(curl --location https://taskfile.dev/install.sh)" -- -d -b "$HOME/.local/bin"
            echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> "$BASH_ENV"

  # GoReleaser's dockers_v2 pipe shells out to `docker buildx build`, so the
  # builder and the registry login have to exist before it runs.
  setup-docker:
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Register QEMU for cross-architecture builds
          # Dockerfile.alpine RUNs `apk add`, once per platform in the manifest,
          # so building its arm64 half on an amd64 host needs binfmt handlers
          # registered. Idempotent, and a no-op for the cimg/base image, which
          # only COPYs.
          command: docker run --privileged --rm tonistiigi/binfmt --install arm64
      - run:
          name: Create a buildx builder
          # The machine image's default buildx driver is `docker`, which can
          # neither build for two platforms in one invocation nor push a
          # manifest list. A docker-container driver can do both.
          command: docker buildx create --use --driver docker-container
      - run:
          name: Log in to Docker Hub
          # Absent on branch dry-runs, which have no context: the snapshot build
          # still exercises the Dockerfile, it just pushes nothing.
          command: |
            if [ -z "${DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME:-}" ]; then
              echo "No Docker Hub credentials — skipping login (snapshot builds do not push)."
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "$DOCKER_HUB_PASSWORD" | docker login --username "$DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME" --password-stdin

  store_results:
    steps:
      - store_test_results:
          path: ./test-reports

executors:
  linux:
    machine:
      image: ubuntu-2604:current
    resource_class: large.gen3

  # Arm64 counterpart to `linux`, for checking both halves of a multi-arch
  # image. Deliberately small: it only pulls and runs a container.
  linux-arm:
    machine:
      image: ubuntu-2604:current
    resource_class: arm.medium

  macos:
    macos:
      xcode: 26.5.0

  windows:
    machine: true
    resource_class: windows.medium

jobs:
  check:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:check
      - store_results

  test:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:test
      - store_results

  mark-release:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Plan deployment
          command: |
            circleci run release plan "${CIRCLE_JOB}" \
              --environment-name="default" \
              --component-name="${CIRCLE_PROJECT_REPONAME}" \
              --target-version="1.0.${CIRCLE_BUILD_NUM}-${CIRCLE_SHA1:0:7}"
      - run:
          name: Update deployment status to running
          command: circleci run release update "${CIRCLE_JOB}" --status=RUNNING
      - run:
          name: Update deployment status to success
          command: circleci run release update "${CIRCLE_JOB}" --status=SUCCESS
          when: on_success
      - run:
          name: Update deployment status to failed
          command: circleci run release update "${CIRCLE_JOB}" --status=FAILED
          when: on_fail

  deploy:
    executor: linux
    parameters:
      publish_steps:
        type: steps
        default:
          - run: task ci:release
    steps:
      - setup
      - setup-docker
      - run: sudo apt update --yes
      - run:
          name: Install snapcraft
          command: |
            sudo apt install snapd --yes
            sudo snap install snapcraft --classic
      - run:
          name: Install choco
          command: |
            sudo cp tools/choco.sh /usr/local/bin/choco
            sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/choco
            choco help
      - steps: << parameters.publish_steps >>
      - store_artifacts:
          path: dist

  smoke-test:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
      install-steps:
        type: steps
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - steps: << parameters.install-steps >>
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci binary
          command: circleci version

  # Matrixed over the executors rather than over the tags: only the architecture
  # needs a machine of its own, so each job checks both variants. Printing the
  # arch inside the container makes the log say which half of the manifest ran. A
  # tag missing this platform fails here anyway — the arm machine images carry no
  # binfmt, so there is nothing to silently emulate an amd64-only image with.
  smoke-test-docker:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci/circleci-cli:v1
          command: docker run --rm circleci/circleci-cli:v1 sh -c 'uname -m; circleci version'
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci/circleci-cli:v1-alpine
          command: docker run --rm circleci/circleci-cli:v1-alpine sh -c 'uname -m; circleci version'

  docs:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run:
          name: Generate reference and build the site
          command: task docs:build
      - run:
          name: Check internal links
          command: task docs:test
      - store_artifacts:
          path: docs/website/public
      - persist_to_workspace:
          root: .
          paths:
            - "docs/website/public"

  docs-publish:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - attach_workspace:
          at: .
      - run:
          name: Publish to gh-pages
          command: task ci:docs:publish

  ok-to-deploy:
    type: no-op

workflows:
  ci:
    jobs:
      # gh-pages holds only generated HTML — never run CI on it. Entry jobs (no
      # `requires`) must opt out explicitly; downstream jobs are gated by these.

      - check:
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - test:
          matrix:
            parameters:
              executor:
                - linux
                - macos
                - windows
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - docs:
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - deploy:
          name: dry-run
          publish_steps:
            - run: task ci:build
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore:
                - main
                - gh-pages

      - ok-to-deploy:
          requires:
            - check
            - test
            - docs
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - mark-release:
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy

      - deploy:
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/deploy
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release
            - macos-codesigning

      - docs-publish:
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/docs-publish
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-snap
          executor: linux
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install snapd
                command: sudo apt update --yes && sudo apt install snapd --yes
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Snap stable channel
                # /snap/bin has to be prepended, not just present: the machine
                # image ships its own circleci in /usr/local/bin, which would
                # otherwise shadow the snap and make this job verify the build
                # agent's CLI instead of the release.
                command: |
                  sudo snap install circleci
                  echo 'export PATH="/snap/bin:$PATH"' >> "$BASH_ENV"
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-brew
          executor: macos
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Homebrew preview tap
                command: |
                  brew update
                  rm -f /opt/homebrew/bin/circleci
                  brew install circleci-public/circleci/circleci@next
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test-docker:
          matrix:
            parameters:
              executor:
                - linux
                - linux-arm
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-choco
          executor: windows
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Chocolatey
                command: choco install circleci-cli -y
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

version: '3'

vars:
  RESULTS_DIR: test-reports
  TEST_REPORT: test-reports/tests.xml
  LINT_REPORT: test-reports/lint.xml

  # Hugo project lives in docs/website/; built output lands in docs/website/public.
  SITE_DIR: docs/website
  SITE_OUT: docs/website/public

  GH_NAME: 'circleci'
  GH_EMAIL: 'ops+deploy-bot@circleci.com'

  # Release version. Every merge to main tags and publishes, so the patch
  # component is the CI build number: unique and monotonically increasing
  # without any manual bookkeeping. Bump RELEASE_SERIES for a minor or major
  # release — 1.1.<build> sorts above every 1.0.<build> under semver.
  #
  # No pre-release suffix: these are full releases, marked latest on GitHub and
  # published to the stable channel of every package manager.
  RELEASE_SERIES: '1.0'
  RELEASE_VERSION: 'v{{.RELEASE_SERIES}}.{{env "CIRCLE_BUILD_NUM" | default "0"}}'

tasks:
  build:
    desc: Build the circleci binary
    vars:
      DEST: '{{default "dist/circleci" .DEST}}'
      COMMIT:
        sh: git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown
      DIRTY:
        sh: test -z "$(git status --porcelain 2>/dev/null)" || echo .dirty
      VERSION: '1.0.0-dev+{{.COMMIT}}{{.DIRTY}}'
    cmds:
      - go build -ldflags="-X main.version={{.VERSION}}" -o "{{.DEST}}" ./cmd/circleci

  release-check:
    desc: Check if the release is ready to be published
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile tools/go.mod goreleaser check

  test:
    desc: Run unit tests
    # clikit is a separate module, so ./... does not reach it. A relative
    # ./clikit/... is rejected as outside the main module, but the module path
    # resolves through the replace in go.mod.
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "./... github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/clikit/..." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile tools/go.mod gotestsum -- -race -count=1 {{.ARGS}}

  check:
    desc: Run all static checks
    cmds:
      - task: fmt
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: ./... --diff
      - task: fmt:clikit
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: ./... --diff
      - task: lint
      - task: lint:clikit
      - task: license
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: -check .
      - task: mod-tidy
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: -diff
      - task: release-check

  fix:
    desc: Auto-fix static checks
    cmds:
      - task: fmt
      - task: fmt:clikit
      - task: license
      - task: mod-tidy
      - task: lint
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: ./... --fix
      - task: lint:clikit
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: ./... --fix

  lint:
    desc: Run golangci-lint
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "./..." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile tools/go.mod golangci-lint run {{.ARGS}}

  lint:clikit:
    desc: Run golangci-lint on the clikit module
    dir: clikit
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "./..." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile ../tools/go.mod golangci-lint run {{.ARGS}}

  fmt:
    desc: Format the code
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "./..." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile tools/go.mod golangci-lint fmt {{.ARGS}}

  fmt:clikit:
    desc: Format the clikit module
    dir: clikit
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "./..." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile ../tools/go.mod golangci-lint fmt {{.ARGS}}

  license:
    desc: Manage license headers
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - |
        go tool -modfile tools/go.mod addlicense \
          -c "Circle Internet Services, Inc." \
          -l mit \
          -s \
          -ignore ".idea/**" \
          -ignore ".circleci/**" \
          -ignore ".claude/**" \
          -ignore ".git/**" \
          -ignore ".github/**" \
          -ignore "test-reports/**" \
          -ignore "**/*.html" \
          -ignore "acceptance/testdata/**" \
          -ignore "bin/**" \
          -ignore "dist/**" \
          -ignore "docs/website/content/**" \
          -ignore "docs/website/public/**" \
          {{.ARGS}}

  mod-tidy:
    desc: Run 'go mod tidy'
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "-v" .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go mod tidy {{.ARGS}}
      - go -C clikit mod tidy {{.ARGS}}
      - go -C tools mod tidy {{.ARGS}}

  mod-download:
    desc: Run 'go mod download'
    cmds:
      - go mod download
      - go -C clikit mod download
      - go mod download -modfile tools/go.mod

  dev-install:
    desc: Build from source and install to ~/.local/bin
    vars:
      DEST: '${HOME}/.local/bin'
    cmds:
      - mkdir -p "{{.DEST}}"
      - task: build
        vars:
          DEST: '{{.DEST}}/circleci'

  generate:
    desc: Run go generate
    cmds:
      - go generate ./...

  # Demo tasks
  #
  # Static PNG/SVG screenshots of the CLI in action are captured with
  # charmbracelet/freeze. Animated GIFs are recorded with charmbracelet/vhs
  # (pinned in tools/go.mod alongside freeze), which additionally needs ttyd,
  # ffmpeg, and the demo font at record time — run `task demo:install` once
  # to install them.
  #
  # The vhs tapes in docs/demos/*.tape run the freshly built dist/circleci
  # against real data, so record while logged in — each tape's header comment
  # explains any per-tape prep (e.g. logging out first for auth-login, or
  # substituting a real run id).

  demo:
    desc: Generate all README/docs screenshots
    cmds:
      - task: demo:run-get-png

  demo:run-get-png:
    desc: Capture a macOS-style PNG and SVG of `circleci run get -b main`
    cmds:
      - for: ['svg']
        cmd: >-
          CIRCLE_NO_PAGER=1 CIRCLE_SPINNER_DISABLED=1
          go tool -modfile tools/go.mod freeze
          --config docs/demos/freeze.json
          --execute "go run ./cmd/circleci run get -b main"
          --execute.timeout 60s
          --output docs/demos/run-get.{{.ITEM}}

  demo:install:
    desc: Install the recording dependencies for the VHS demos (ttyd, ffmpeg, JetBrains Mono)
    cmds:
      - brew install ttyd ffmpeg
      # vhs records in a headless browser, so the demo font must be installed
      # system-wide (the copy bundled inside JetBrains IDEs is not visible to it).
      - brew install --cask font-jetbrains-mono

  demo:gifs:
    desc: Record all animated GIF demos with VHS (requires ttyd + ffmpeg)
    deps: [build]
    cmds:
      - for: ['auth-login', 'run-list-get', 'run-get-tui', 'setting-theme', 'run-get-jq']
        cmd: PATH="$PWD/dist:$PATH" go tool -modfile tools/go.mod vhs docs/demos/{{.ITEM}}.tape

  demo:gif:
    desc: 'Record a single demo tape by name, e.g.: task demo:gif -- run-get-tui'
    deps: [build]
    cmds:
      - PATH="$PWD/dist:$PATH" go tool -modfile tools/go.mod vhs docs/demos/{{.CLI_ARGS}}.tape

  extensions:install:
    desc: Install known official extensions
    cmds:
      - go run ./cmd/circleci extension install testsuite

  docs:reference:
    desc: Generate the reference page from the live command tree
    deps:
      - extensions:install
    cmds:
      - mkdir -p {{.SITE_DIR}}/content/reference {{.SITE_DIR}}/static/img
      # The landing page (/) is a hand-written template; the screenshot it shows
      # is the freeze-captured demo, copied into the site's static tree.
      - cp docs/demos/run-get.svg {{.SITE_DIR}}/static/img/run-get.svg
      # Generate the help-topic bodies once, then derive three artifacts:
      #
      #   static/llms.txt             — the short index llmstxt.org actually
      #                                 describes: getting started (install,
      #                                 authenticate, MCP) plus links out. This
      #                                 file used to be the full dump, which cost
      #                                 an agent ~50k tokens to answer "how do I
      #                                 install this?" — and then sent it to the
      #                                 README anyway. Keep it small.
      #   static/llms-full.txt        — every topic plus the whole command tree,
      #                                 for agents that need command detail.
      #   content/reference/_index.md — the same full body with Hugo front
      #                                 matter, served at /reference.
      #
      # Hugo copies static/ to the site root verbatim. Both .txt files open with
      # an H1 + blockquote summary per the llms.txt spec.
      - |
        GS="$(mktemp)"
        REST="$(mktemp)"
        go run ./cmd/circleci help getting-started > "$GS"
        {
          go run ./cmd/circleci help environment
          echo
          go run ./cmd/circleci help formatting
          echo
          go run ./cmd/circleci help reference
        } > "$REST"

        {
          echo '# CircleCI CLI'
          echo
          echo '> Command-line interface to CircleCI for use in your terminal or scripts. This is the short index: install, authenticate, and links to the full reference.'
          echo
          cat "$GS"
          echo
          echo '## Reference'
          echo
          echo '- [Full command reference](https://cli.circleci.com/llms-full.txt): every command, flag and JSON field, generated from the live command tree. Large — fetch it when you need command detail.'
          echo '- [Command reference on the web](https://cli.circleci.com/reference/): the same content as a browsable page.'
          echo '- [Environment variables](https://cli.circleci.com/reference/#environment): authentication, colour, paging and telemetry. Also `circleci help environment`.'
          echo '- [Output formatting](https://cli.circleci.com/reference/#formatting): `--json`, `--jq` and templates. Also `circleci help formatting`.'
          echo '- [Source, issue tracker and prebuilt binaries](https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli)'
        } > {{.SITE_DIR}}/static/llms.txt

        {
          echo '# CircleCI CLI'
          echo
          echo '> Command-line interface to CircleCI for use in your terminal or scripts. This is the full command reference, generated from the live command tree. The short index is at https://cli.circleci.com/llms.txt'
          echo
          cat "$GS"
          echo
          cat "$REST"
        } > {{.SITE_DIR}}/static/llms-full.txt

        {
          echo '---'
          echo 'title: CircleCI CLI Reference'
          echo '---'
          echo
          cat "$GS"
          echo
          cat "$REST"
        } > {{.SITE_DIR}}/content/reference/_index.md

        rm -f "$GS" "$REST"

  docs:clean:
    desc: Remove the built docs site
    cmds:
      - rm -rf {{.SITE_OUT}}

  docs:build:
    desc: Generate the reference and build the static site
    deps:
      - docs:clean
      - docs:reference
    cmds:
      - 'go tool -modfile tools/go.mod hugo --source {{.SITE_DIR}} --minify --gc'

  docs:server:
    desc: Serve the docs site locally with live reload
    deps:
      - docs:reference
    cmds:
      - 'go tool -modfile tools/go.mod hugo server --source {{.SITE_DIR}} {{.CLI_ARGS}}'

  docs:test:
    desc: Validate the built site's internal links with htmltest
    cmds:
      - 'go tool -modfile tools/go.mod htmltest -c {{.SITE_DIR}}/.htmltest.yml {{.CLI_ARGS}}'

  docs:hugo:
    desc: Run the pinned Hugo binary with arbitrary arguments
    cmds:
      - 'go tool -modfile tools/go.mod hugo --source {{.SITE_DIR}} {{.CLI_ARGS}}'

  ci:docs:publish:
    desc: Publish the built site to the gh-pages branch (CI only)
    vars:
      BRANCH: gh-pages
      WORKTREE: .gh-pages
      MESSAGE: 'Deploy docs from {{env "CIRCLE_SHA1" | default "local"}}'
    cmds:
      - test -d {{.SITE_OUT}} || { echo "Run 'task docs:build' first."; exit 1; }
      # Only set the deploy-bot identity in CI; never clobber a local git config.
      - |
        if [ -n "${CI:-}" ]; then
          git config --global user.email '{{.GH_EMAIL}}'
          git config --global user.name '{{.GH_NAME}}'
        fi
      - rm -rf {{.WORKTREE}}
      - git worktree prune
      - |
        git fetch origin {{.BRANCH}} || true
        if git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/remotes/origin/{{.BRANCH}}; then
          git worktree add -B {{.BRANCH}} {{.WORKTREE}} origin/{{.BRANCH}}
        else
          git worktree add --orphan -b {{.BRANCH}} {{.WORKTREE}}
        fi
      # Replace the branch's contents wholesale so deletions propagate, then copy
      # in the freshly built site (the .git pointer file must survive).
      - find {{.WORKTREE}} -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name .git -exec rm -rf {} +
      - cp -R {{.SITE_OUT}}/. {{.WORKTREE}}/
      - |
        git -C {{.WORKTREE}} add -A
        git -C {{.WORKTREE}} commit -m '{{.MESSAGE}}' || { echo "No changes to publish."; }
        git -C {{.WORKTREE}} push origin {{.BRANCH}}
      - git worktree remove --force {{.WORKTREE}}

  # CI tasks

  ci:lint:
    desc: Lint with JUnit output
    cmds:
      - mkdir -p "{{.RESULTS_DIR}}"
      - task: lint
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: |
            ./... \
            --output.junit-xml.path "{{.LINT_REPORT}}" --output.junit-xml.extended \
            --output.text.path=stdout --output.text.colors=true

  ci:test:
    desc: Run tests with JUnit output
    vars:
      NAME: '{{if not (eq OS "windows")}}ci tests{{else}}windows tests{{end}}'
    cmds:
      - mkdir -p {{.RESULTS_DIR}}
      - circleci testsuite run "{{.NAME}}"

  ci:check:
    desc: Check no uncommitted diffs after generate/fmt/tidy
    cmds:
      - task: fmt
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: ./... --diff
      - task: fmt:clikit
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: ./... --diff
      - task: ci:lint
      - task: lint:clikit
      - task: license
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: -check .
      - task: mod-tidy
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: -diff
      - task: release-check
      - task: generate
      - git diff --exit-code

  ci:release:
    desc: Tag, build, and publish a release
    vars:
      VERSION: '{{.RELEASE_VERSION}}'
    cmds:
      # Only set the deploy-bot identity in CI; never clobber a local git config.
      - |
        if [ -n "${CI:-}" ]; then
          git config --global user.email '{{.GH_EMAIL}}'
          git config --global user.name '{{.GH_NAME}}'
        fi
      - git tag -a '{{.VERSION}}' -m 'Release {{.VERSION}}'
      - git push origin '{{.VERSION}}'
      - go tool -modfile tools/go.mod goreleaser release --clean
      - task: ci:packagecloud
      - task: ci:cloudsmith
      - task: ci:virustotal
      - task: ci:tag-clikit

  ci:tag-clikit:
    desc: Tag the clikit module so extension authors can 'go get' this release
    vars:
      TAG: 'clikit/{{.RELEASE_VERSION}}'
    cmds:
      # Only set the deploy-bot identity in CI; never clobber a local git config.
      - |
        if [ -n "${CI:-}" ]; then
          git config --global user.email '{{.GH_EMAIL}}'
          git config --global user.name '{{.GH_NAME}}'
        fi
      - git tag -a '{{.TAG}}' -m 'Release {{.TAG}}'
      - git push origin '{{.TAG}}'

  ci:virustotal:
    desc: Submit the release artifacts in dist/ to VirusTotal for scanning
    # VT_APIKEY must be set in the environment to actually upload; without it the
    # step logs a skip and exits 0. Submission is best-effort and never gates the
    # release — VirusTotal frequently false-flags Go binaries. Set DRY_RUN to list
    # the artifacts without contacting VirusTotal.
    vars:
      DRY_RUN: '{{default "" .DRY_RUN}}'
    cmds:
      # Submit what users actually download: the archives and the Linux packages.
      # VirusTotal unpacks archives and scans the contained binaries.
      - go run ./cmd/virustotal submit {{if .DRY_RUN}}--dry-run {{end}}dist/*.tar.gz dist/*.zip dist/*.deb dist/*.rpm

  ci:packagecloud:
    desc: Publish the Linux nfpm packages (rpm + deb) from dist/ to packagecloud
    # PACKAGECLOUD_TOKEN must be set in the environment (not needed when DRY_RUN is
    # set). Override REPO to target a different packagecloud repository
    # (<user>/<repo>); set DRY_RUN to validate without uploading.
    vars:
      REPO: '{{default "circleci/circleci" .REPO}}'
      DRY_RUN: '{{default "" .DRY_RUN}}'
    cmds:
      # goreleaser only pushes to packagecloud under a Pro licence, so cmd/packagecloud
      # uploads the nfpm output to the public REST API instead — no Ruby CLI needed.
      - go run ./cmd/packagecloud pkg push {{if .DRY_RUN}}--dry-run {{end}}--repo '{{.REPO}}' dist/*.rpm dist/*.deb

  ci:cloudsmith:
    desc: Publish the Linux nfpm packages (deb + rpm) from dist/ to Cloudsmith
    # CLOUDSMITH_API_KEY must be set in the environment (not needed when DRY_RUN is
    # set). Override CLOUDSMITH_REPO to target a different Cloudsmith repository
    # (<owner>/<repo>); set DRY_RUN to validate without uploading.
    vars:
      CLOUDSMITH_REPO: '{{default "circleci-deps/public" .CLOUDSMITH_REPO}}'
      DRY_RUN: '{{default "" .DRY_RUN}}'
    cmds:
      # goreleaser can't push to Cloudsmith without a Pro licence, so cmd/cloudsmith
      # uploads the nfpm output to the public REST API instead. Every package is
      # published to the generic "any-distro/any-version" distribution.
      - go run ./cmd/cloudsmith push deb {{if .DRY_RUN}}--dry-run {{end}}--repo '{{.CLOUDSMITH_REPO}}' dist/*.deb
      - go run ./cmd/cloudsmith push rpm {{if .DRY_RUN}}--dry-run {{end}}--repo '{{.CLOUDSMITH_REPO}}' dist/*.rpm

  ci:build:
    desc: Dry-run a release — build a snapshot (incl. nfpms) and dry-run the packagecloud publish
    vars:
      VERSION: '{{.RELEASE_VERSION}}'
    cmds:
      # Only set the deploy-bot identity in CI; never clobber a local git config.
      - |
        if [ -n "${CI:-}" ]; then
          git config --global user.email '{{.GH_EMAIL}}'
          git config --global user.name '{{.GH_NAME}}'
        fi
      - git tag -a '{{.VERSION}}' -m 'Release {{.VERSION}}'
      - go tool -modfile tools/go.mod goreleaser release --snapshot --skip=snapcraft --skip=chocolatey --clean
      - task: ci:packagecloud
        vars:
          DRY_RUN: "true"
      - task: ci:cloudsmith
        vars:
          DRY_RUN: "true"
      - task: ci:virustotal
        vars:
          DRY_RUN: "true"
